$:set -eu
echo "=== ROOT README ==="
if test -f README.md; then cat README.md; else echo "ROOT README ABSENT"; fi
echo "=== ROOT AGENTS ==="
cat AGENTS.md
echo "=== TASK INSTRUCTIONS ==="
find Tasks -maxdepth 3 \( -iname 'AGENTS.md' -o -iname 'README.md' \) -type f -print
echo "=== TASK TREE ==="
find Tasks -maxdepth 3 -type f | sort | head -120
echo "=== RECENT TASK EXAMPLE ==="
find Tasks -maxdepth 3 -type f \( -name '*.json' -o -name '*.md' \) | sort | tail -12 | while IFS= read -r f; do echo "--- $f"; head -c 2400 "$f"; echo; done
echo "=== DESIGN PROJECT INSTRUCTIONS ==="
if test -f workspaces/codespace-mcp-srs-design/README.md; then cat workspaces/codespace-mcp-srs-design/README.md; fi
if test -f workspaces/codespace-mcp-srs-design/AGENTS.md; then cat workspaces/codespace-mcp-srs-design/AGENTS.md; fi
echo "=== METADATA ==="
if test -f config/file-metadata.json; then head -c 1200 config/file-metadata.json; else echo "NOT PRESENT"; fi
outputThat: **Structural boundary:** Part I contains exclusively mandatory SHALL imperatives. Part II contains independently organized SHOULD procedures, concrete examples and descriptive contract facts. Procedures do not grant authority or override imperatives.
"shall": "The agent shall read the current applicable repository documentation and active interface contract before performing a repository operation."
"shall": "The agent shall identify the currently implemented interface for the requested function instead of relying on historical, proposed, or disabled interfaces."
"shall": "The agent shall preserve the full user-requested scope, authorized resources, and intended final state."
"shall": "The agent shall use the prescribed Terminals interface for operations it supports."
"shall": "The agent shall recheck applicable implementation and contracts when the repository revision changes."
"shall": "The agent shall not silently substitute another route or repeat a failed non-idempotent operation."
"shall": "The agent shall confine every mutation and execution to the task's authorized repository, Issue, project and workspace."
"shall": "The agent shall comply with the selected interface's source identity, event type, full input schema, allowed paths and execution constraints."
"shall": "The agent shall submit Issue #3 commands as complete JSON-object Issue comments with nonblank runOn, whatPrompt and forWhom strings."
"shall": "The agent shall use only '$' or 'gh' for Issue #3 runOn and a distinct safe forWhom nonce complying with the current documented nonce format."
"shall": "The agent shall not use a pull-request comment or an unregistered Issue as a substitute for the specified execution input."
"shall": "The agent shall verify that any Issue #10 RuntimeConfig execution route actually exists before using the Issue #10 new-comment contract."
"shall": "The agent shall match all non-metadata keys, nested structures and types of the selected RuntimeConfig template and shall omit metadata from its set object."
"shall": "The agent shall reject missing, surplus, null, blank or otherwise invalid template values and paths that violate workspace, traversal, existence or symlink restrictions."
"shall": "The agent shall express typed source-template substitutions with unquoted <name> tokens, runtime variables or expressions with unquoted $name tokens, and quoted strings only for literals."
"shall": "The agent shall compile and safely serialize source templates before sending JSON and shall not submit uncompiled template syntax or concatenate untrusted text into executable source."
"shall": "The agent shall limit direct GitHub integration activity to the expressly permitted tools, operations and repository resource scopes in the access procedure."
"shall": "The agent shall use direct integration for workflow-file read, creation, update and deletion only within .github/workflows/*.yml or .github/workflows/*.yaml."
"shall": "The agent shall not modify workflow files through current Terminals command interfaces."
"shall": "The agent shall confine direct integration Issue-comment operations to Issue comments, excluding pull-request comments."
"shall": "The agent shall access workspaces/terminalruns/** read-only through the permitted direct integration file reader."
"shall": "The agent shall limit direct integration Actions operations to the specified inspection, artifact and rerun tools for BestNameYet/Terminals."
"shall": "The agent shall not use unlisted direct integration tools, paths or operations."
"shall": "The agent shall associate each submission with its source comment ID, nonce, workflow run and attempt, output path and available execution receipt or commit."
"shall": "The agent shall independently verify requested target state before claiming completion."
"shall": "The agent shall distinguish successful comment submission, command execution, persisted stdout, downstream execution and final publication."
"shall": "The agent shall inspect Issue #3 stdout in workspaces/terminalruns/** and the corresponding Actions job data for stderr and exit status."

"shall": "The agent shall verify a shared-conversation extraction using the extractor run conclusion, eight required files, receipt hashes and sizes, remote byte readback and final verified attestation."
"shall": "The agent shall not classify an inaccessible, incompatible or unparseable shared-conversation source as a successful extraction."
"shall": "The agent shall read back the full target Issue or Issue-comment body after a writer mutation."
"shall": "The agent shall preserve the existing body explicitly when an append is requested through a replacement-only writer."
"shall": "The agent shall report failures, partial outcomes and unverified claims without equating an accepted command, saved stdout file or success label with user-task completion."
"shall": "The agent shall stop at unavailable or unverified execution paths rather than inventing syntax, authorization, results or alternate routes."

Procedures are organized by **operational task**, not by imperative categories or identifiers. Each procedure provides the entry point, steps, syntax and examples needed to carry out applicable rules. Procedures do not grant authorization independently of the imperatives. Interface-specific source contracts remain authoritative for their current syntax.
1. The agent SHOULD inspect the current revision, applicable README and AGENTS documents, target Issue's contract, workflow source and .github/issue-workflow-registry.json.
2. The agent SHOULD verify each route against the current Git tree rather than treating an old Issue description as proof of a deployed workflow.
3. The agent SHOULD distinguish an input router, an execution workflow and the downstream program. A configured trigger SHOULD not be equated with completed work.
4. The agent SHOULD use Issue #3 for supported repository reads or commands, then obtain its committed terminal output and inspect results.
| Shell/GitHub CLI | Owner-authored Issue #3 comment, created or edited | Active, via registered listener |
| RuntimeConfig Node.js | Issue #10 newly created comment with runpath/set | Documented but inactive: named workflow absent; registry has no route |
| Shared-conversation extractor | Specialized extractor program | Present; some source pages fail decoding |
| Issue writers | Programs in workspaces/RuntimeConfig | Files/templates exist; execution route requires verification |
| Other reserved Issues | Registry-specific | No executable route inferred from Issue number |

1. The agent SHOULD follow the Programs selection source-language convention, version 0.2.0: unquoted <name> is a typed placeholder resolved at instantiation; unquoted $name or $options[$id].id is a runtime binding/expression; quoted text is literal.
2. The agent SHOULD treat source templates as intermediate, intentionally non-JSON representations and safely encode each supplied value according to its required type.

3. The agent SHOULD serialize the final value as valid JSON before submitting it to an Issue. If a consumer supports runtime expressions, the agent SHOULD use that interface's encoding instead of passing the uncompiled $... expression through JSON.parse.
4. The agent SHOULD check the distinction between template runtime references and Bash variable substitution when a generated command invokes a shell.
**Syntax reference:** workspaces/programs/selection-element-specification.md, v0.2.0. Source templates SHOULD never be presented as valid JSON until instantiated and serialized.

1. The agent SHOULD consult https://github.com/BestNameYet/Terminals/issues/3 immediately before submission. Its current required fields are runOn, whatPrompt and forWhom; the complete Issue-comment body is one JSON object.

2. The agent SHOULD use '$' for Bash or 'gh' for GitHub CLI command semantics. The current runner invokes Bash with pipefail, from GITHUB_WORKSPACE, with a 300-second command timeout and a 64-MiB stdout buffer.

3. The agent SHOULD submit a new owner-authored comment or intentionally edit one when that event is appropriate. Both actions can trigger execution; the interface does not guarantee FIFO ordering across independent commands.
4. The agent SHOULD identify the comment ID, router run and terminal run, then retrieve the timestamped workspaces/terminalruns/<forWhom>_<UTCtimestamp>.json named by resultPath.

5. The agent SHOULD inspect inputThis and outputThat as the echoed command and stdout line array. The agent SHOULD check Actions for stderr, exit status, process errors and the result-path/commit record.
6. The agent SHOULD verify the intended target state separately and distinguish a nonzero command with persisted stdout from a successful command.
**Expected stdout receipt shape for that example:**

1. The agent SHOULD confirm that the intended Issue #10 workflow is present and enabled; the Issue body alone is not sufficient. During this revision, .github/workflows/issue-10-runtimeconfig.yml was absent and the registry entry for Issue #10 was empty.

2. Once a route is active, the agent SHOULD read workspaces/RuntimeConfig/<runpath>/runtrigger.json and the selected program before composing a **new** Issue #10 comment. The documented route uses created, not edited, comments.

3. The agent SHOULD populate runpath with an existing RuntimeConfig subfolder and set with exactly the template's non-metadata keys and nested types. The template's metadata SHOULD be left out of set so the runtime can preserve it.
4. The agent SHOULD follow the exact field spelling of the selected template. Existing writer templates use jsPath, whereas an older Issue #10 example uses js_path; the template SHOULD control.

5. Where deployed, the agent SHOULD inspect the generated runtrigger_<commentID>_issue10_<timestamp>.json, its push receipt, the Node.js execution, logs and artifacts. The runner passes the program one JSON.stringify(args) argument.
6. The agent SHOULD not interpret acceptance of an Issue comment as running a missing workflow. An unavailable route SHOULD be reported as a dependency, not bypassed.
**Source command template for a template having jsPath and args:**
**Instantiated example using the current issue-body-writer template (illustrative; not for submission while the route is inactive):**

1. The agent SHOULD inspect the current source and trigger template of workspaces/RuntimeConfig/issue-comment-writer/ or workspaces/RuntimeConfig/issue-body-writer/ before running either program through an authorized available entry point.
2. For the comment writer, the agent SHOULD use commentId="new" for creation or an existing positive decimal comment ID for replacement, after checking target ownership.
3. The agent SHOULD supply issuePath identifying the exact Issue and jsonArrayPath containing either a repository-readable JSON-array path or a serialized JSON array permitted by the program.
4. The agent SHOULD build a nonempty array of nonempty objects whose values are strings. These writers concatenate values in array/object iteration order, separating values by two newlines.
5. For append requests, the agent SHOULD read the old complete body and include it in the new complete replacement body. The programs are full-body replacement writers, not append writers.
6. After execution, the agent SHOULD independently read the destination body and verify complete content and target identity.
**Instantiation example for new-comment creation, only after verifying route and template:**
1. The agent SHOULD inspect the live extractor contract in Issue #3, the extractor workflow and workspaces/extractor-srs-design/runtime/ before submitting a URL.

2. The agent SHOULD pass a public HTTPS chatgpt.com/share/<share_uuid> URL through canonical request_json, with optional write_path, request_id and export_profile, or use the documented mutually exclusive legacy inputs.
3. The agent SHOULD use export_profile "complete" if supplied, omit unknown request keys and keep custom output under workspaces/shared-conversations/.
4. The agent SHOULD submit the serialized request through the authorized Terminals command interface, then correlate the terminal receipt with the actual extractor run ID.

5. The agent SHOULD inspect the extractor run, its output directory, the eight required files, SHA-256/size metadata, remote-main byte equality and external final publication attestation recording VERIFIED and the commit.
6. The agent SHOULD treat an unrecognized serialization stream or inaccessible share as a failure of extraction rather than a failure of the prior terminal command.
7. The agent SHOULD consider that the workflow publishes raw captured HTML and the conversation text into durable repository storage.
**Instantiated example with a previously successful public share:**

**Expected output filenames:** response.html, conversation-raw.json, linear-conversation.json, conversation.json, conversation.md, diagnostics.json, receipt.json and execution.json. The agent SHOULD obtain a separate final verified publication attestation; precommit output alone is not sufficient.
### 7. Apply the direct GitHub integration allowlist
1. The agent SHOULD use Terminals for operations supported there, and SHOULD limit exceptions to the precise tool/resource pairs below, all confined to BestNameYet/Terminals.
2. The agent SHOULD use only the listed Issue comment tools for Issue comment reads or writes and avoid PR comments.

3. The agent SHOULD use the listed file tools for workflow YAML files at the restricted paths. Current Terminals cannot modify workflow files; the direct integration route is the authorized exception.
4. The agent SHOULD use the terminal-result read exception only for persisted workspaces/terminalruns/** output, not general source-file access.
5. The agent SHOULD use listed Actions tools only for job inspection, artifacts and reruns in the specified repository.
6. The agent SHOULD independently verify outcomes after an allowed integration mutation.
| Domain | Allowed tools | Permitted resource | Access |
| Issue comments | mcp__GitHub__fetch_issue_comments, mcp__GitHub__add_comment_to_issue, mcp__GitHub__update_issue_comment | Issue comments only; no PR comments | read/create/update |

| Workflow YAML | mcp__GitHub__fetch_file, mcp__GitHub__create_file, mcp__GitHub__update_file, mcp__GitHub__delete_file | .github/workflows/*.yml and .github/workflows/*.yaml | read/create/update/delete |
| Actions jobs | mcp__GitHub__fetch_workflow_run_jobs, mcp__GitHub__fetch_workflow_job_steps, mcp__GitHub__fetch_workflow_job_logs | repository Actions jobs | read |
| Actions artifacts | mcp__GitHub__fetch_workflow_run_artifacts, mcp__GitHub__download_workflow_artifact | repository Actions artifacts | read/download |
| Actions reruns | mcp__GitHub__rerun_workflow_job, mcp__GitHub__rerun_failed_workflow_run_jobs | repository Actions runs | rerun |

The future target is direct integration Issue-comment create/edit only, with other capabilities routed through authorized repository workflows. The agent SHOULD not infer that this future restriction is already technically enforced.

1. The agent SHOULD trace the relevant sequence **source input → Issue comment → registered listener → command run → terminal output → downstream operation → final state**, omitting inapplicable stages rather than inventing success.
2. The agent SHOULD record comment ID, nonce, run ID, run attempt, result path, output commit, artifact name, destination and any final attestation.

3. The agent SHOULD inspect execution receipts and Actions results as evidence of specific stages. For source-file changes, the agent SHOULD verify published path, bytes and commit; for Issue mutations, the agent SHOULD re-fetch the complete body.
4. The agent SHOULD distinguish authorization errors, JSON/schema rejection, command/runtime failure, missing workflow, downstream program errors, publication failure and verification failure.
5. The agent SHOULD avoid automatic replays of non-idempotent commands; a retry SHOULD follow a documented recovery method and current authority.
6. The agent SHOULD report verified successes and failures separately.

**Example:** An Issue #3 terminal command can exit successfully and persist a receipt containing a downstream extractor run URL. That extractor can subsequently fail with MISSING_STREAM. The agent SHOULD report successful command execution and failed extraction as distinct outcomes.

The wrapper is the outermost JSON **array**, not an object. Every outer element preceding the last is either an individual standalone rule or an array containing a single subject group. The last **outer** element gives interpretation instructions for the outer array.

In each grouped array, index **0** has the same interpretation function locally that the last outer index has globally: it specifies that group's single subject, its scope, and how the remaining group indices are interpreted. Group rule entries occupy indices **1** onward. A group does **not** reserve its final index for interpretation.

Standalone ad hoc rules are ordered newest-to-oldest. Insert each newly adopted standalone rule at **outer index 0** (or index 0 of its applicable ad hoc array); previous indices shift by **+1**. The outermost interpretation element remains last. A group's index 0 remains its subject/scope/interpretation entry when rules are inserted after it.
A nested group's index 0 controls interpretation inside that group. Where it explicitly overrides the outermost interpretation, the local interpretation takes precedence **within that group only**.

The accompanying `Tasks/TasksCompleted/user-prompt-task-1794193447-wrapper.json` contains the existing full user-defined-scope instruction, preserving its wording and behavioral scope, presented as one subject group. No unrelated or invented account instruction was added. Future standalone ad hoc instructions may be inserted as outer elements without changing the single-subject group.

Specify an integrated GitHub Codespaces development environment exposing a Node.js MCP server to ChatGPT, with agent-accessible tools and resources, persistent project files, recoverable task state, and verifiable execution.
- Codespace provisioning, devcontainer configuration, service startup, shutdown, idle behavior, restart and watchdog operation.
- MCP transport, server lifecycle, discovery, tool calls, resource listings, reads and embedded resource delivery.
- Terminal and coding operations, process/session management, stdout, stderr, exit codes, interruption, and persistent workspace state.
- Git repository integration, authorized workspace boundaries, authentication, credential handling, and access controls.
- Applicable `AGENTS.md`, README, specifications, procedures, canonical resource provenance, change detection and task-preparation enforcement.
- Task and session persistence, nonces, ordering, execution receipts, log retention, replay and recovery semantics.
- Security, failure modes, costs, hosting constraints, integration with existing Terminals/CommandLine workflows and migration decisions.
- Automated unit, component, integration and end-to-end validation with independently verified acceptance criteria.
These files are **planned**, not yet created:
- `SRS.agent.json` — independently useful, semantics-first, machine-readable SRS projection.
- `ARCHITECTURE.md` — components, trust boundaries, lifecycle, deployment, and data flows.
- `INTERFACES.md` — MCP resources/tools, request/response contracts, errors and authentication.
- `VERIFICATION-PLAN.md` — requirement-linked tests, acceptance criteria and evidence.

The five-stage bootstrap procedure in `AGENTS.md` covers: (1) authority and material constraints, (2) requirements and semantic projection, (3) architecture and interfaces including decisions and risks, (4) verification, and (5) one consistency/readiness check. There is no separate inventory, feasibility report, risk register, or handoff report. These subjects remain addressed where relevant in the required artifacts.

This workspace contains design artifacts only until implementation is separately authorized. Existing repository execution interfaces and governing procedures remain in force. Proposed capabilities must be distinguished from observed, implemented and independently verified capabilities. Changes must remain scoped to the authorized workspace unless separately approved.
